findings.text: SVSM page validation entry processes a page state descriptor through the secure monitor calling area with native interrupt control and deferred small page retry for size mismatches. It serves as the nested privilege path counterpart to direct validation.

Public SNP memory helpers request shared or private state for a virtual range and accept physical ranges by converting them to a virtual range. Each helper does nothing when the platform lacks SNP guest support.

Central validation dispatcher selects the monitor path when running under a nested privilege level and otherwise uses the direct instruction path. It then applies cache eviction for newly private pages unless a hardware coherency fix is present.
Page state descriptors are consumed inclusively from the first slot through the header end marker. Progress markers must never move backward and reserved header bits must stay clear.
Logical direction derives from the requested operation where private means validate and shared means rescind. The boolean action is stored in monitor entries and guides mitigation.

Large page validation that reports a size mismatch is retried at small granularity covering the same span. The direct path expands inline while the monitor path defers failed large entries and later resubmits them as small ranges.
Any unrecoverable validation error emits a warning diagnostic and then ends the guest through the secure termination path with the Linux set and validation reason.

Monitor validation and monitor call setup save native interrupt state and fetch the per CPU calling area while disabled to avoid migration to another CPU. Saved state is restored afterward with nesting around communication block acquisition.
Page state programming and processor control hold local interrupts across communication block acquisition plus host interaction plus release. This ensures exclusive use per operation.

Descriptors carry a header with current index plus end index plus reserved field and an entry array. Guest entries name a frame plus an operation plus a size selector while monitor entries name a frame plus a boolean action plus a size selector with cleared control fields and counters for total and current position.
Secure monitor core identifiers encode protocol zero in the upper half and the call number in the lower half. Observed uses include validation and virtual CPU creation and deletion.

Validation uses encoding F2 0F 01 FF and permission adjustment uses F3 0F 01 FE with address plus size selector plus request word as operands. Validation reports a distinct no update condition separate from its return code.
A large entry covers the same range as 512 small pages. Eviction and retry logic use that correspondence when expanding a large request.

Page state requests are copied into the shared buffer bounded by its capacity and the host is invoked repeatedly until its progress marker passes the end marker. Warnings and failure occur if error info appears or reserved bits are set or markers regress.

Monitor calls over the communication block invalidate the block and set version and usage and run request with cleared auxiliary info and publish the block address. The flow then issues the request and rejects pending signals and validates exception info and translates result codes while forwarding genuine exceptions.

Host exception reports are accepted only when flagged valid with an exception type and a general or undefined opcode vector. An optional error code lives in the high half and zero status means success while anything else means host error.

Virtualization exception forwarder routes general protection and undefined opcode and page fault and alignment check to their normal handlers with fault address update for page faults. Any other vector is fatal with an emergency message and trap.
Fault address updates have a paravirtual path through the operation table and a native path writing the control register directly. The native form uses a single move with memory ordering.
Frame numbers convert to kernel addresses by shifting to byte offset and applying the direct map base translation.

Calling area selection prefers per CPU storage when enabled and otherwise uses a fixed boot page and its physical address. Early code obtains the boot page through position independent address computation.

Native flag handling saves state with stack operations and disables with clear interrupt and enables with set interrupt. Restore reenables only when the saved image had interrupts enabled as tested via the interrupt flag.

Cache eviction mitigation touches edge bytes of each small page to flush lines across the requested count. An alternate configuration provides an empty operation and the caller skips mitigation when hardware reports no coherency issue.

Range programming clears the descriptor and fills entries from virtual addresses with distinct frame lookup for special mappings versus direct mappings. Large entries are allowed only when aligned with sufficient remainder and validation is rescinded before sharing and performed after privatizing with the new cursor returned.

Range state helper chooses an early direct messaging path when no host block exists and otherwise normalizes alignment and delegates successive chunks to the chunk programmer until the range is covered.

Processor lifecycle control builds a host request combining processor identifier plus privilege level plus event with the control area address and feature flags for creation. It then checks response validity and low half success indicator.

Virtual save area flag handling uses monitor calls for creation and deletion when under a nested privilege level and otherwise adjusts permissions directly targeting a less privileged level. The direct form uses small pages with an optional save area bit.
Host exchange failure or missing communication block ends the guest while processor control failure is reported to the caller. Unsupported forwarded exceptions end with a fatal trap after logging.
Byte copy support includes a compiler intrinsic form plus a 32 bit form using repeated word then byte moves plus a 64 bit form using repeated byte moves with a feature gated fast path.

Page table encryption preparation is inert in this configuration returning success and leaving masks unchanged. Save area cleanup clears the flag and either logs on failure or releases the page on success.

Host communication blocks observed here expose version and usage selectors plus software exit code and info words plus a shared buffer area plus saved exit info and general registers for processor control.
When the security feature is disabled at build time validation and adjustment and cache eviction collapse to trivial success or empty operations.
